Hi Alice — really appreciate the clear asks. Quick summary up front, then a short ops checklist beneath. Looping in Karthik (platform) and Marissa (security/compliance) for technical and legal confirmations.

Summary (high level)
- Deletion via API creates a tombstone immediately; that prevents the record from being returned by runtime reads.
- Tombstone metadata is replicated to other replicas/regions within the same write window (typically seconds to minutes).
- Physical expunge (data removal from snapshot/backups/offline copies) is done by the background GC/expunge pipeline during scheduled waves — default window is 24–72 hours for primary replicas, up to 7 days for immutable offsite snapshots depending on snapshot retention policy.
- Legal hold overrides: if you place an account-level hold before expunge, we mark those snapshots/objects as retained and exclude them from background expunge; we can provide signed audit events and an evidence bundle.

Short operational checklist you can share with audit (high level):
1) Confirm desired retention window and whether immutable snapshots are enabled (GreenBank default?).
2) If immediate removal from backups is required, open a coordinated expunge request with support (see ticket process).
3) For cross-region propagation, list any jurisdictions that require additional approvals.
4) For legal hold: provide hold-id and timeframe — our team will attach hold metadata and produce an evidence package.

Attachments: I attached a short flow diagram (backup-expunge-flow.pdf) and a template MA action-items spreadsheet with required fields for a coordinated expunge.

Hi all — quick technical notes to supplement Logan's summary. I tried to keep this ADA-friendly for auditors.

How deletion flows through our stack:
- Step 1: API delete -> tombstone record written to primary commit log (instant). Tombstone prevents reads and marks the object for GC.
- Step 2: Tombstone replication -> commit replicated to replicas (usually < 1 minute for same-region; cross-region replication depends on routing but often < 10 minutes).
- Step 3: Snapshot & backup retention -> scheduled snapshots are immutable until their TTL expires. If a snapshot taken before deletion contains the object, that snapshot will continue to contain the data until snapshot expiration or manual invalidation.
- Step 4: Background expunge -> we run a distributed expunge job that compacts replicas and prunes tombstoned data. Default cadence is daily; actual expunge of legacy snapshots that were taken pre-deletion can take up to 7 days depending on snapshot retention tier and offsite transfer cadence.

Emergency/accelerated expunge (what we do when a customer requests immediate removal):
- Preconditions: signed authorization + support ticket + account owner confirmation.
- We schedule an expedited compaction and run manual expunge across replicas; cross-region synchronisation is kicked and monitored. Expect a best-effort target of 48–72 hours for full removal from hot/cold replicas; immutable offsite snapshots may still require provider-level retention respect, so worst-case is 7–14 days for full global expunge (we document each step).

Legal hold behavior:
- Holds are additive metadata flags attached to account IDs and snapshots. If a hold is present, expunge jobs skip the affected objects. We can supply a signed hold manifest and an event audit trail (timestamps, job IDs).

Evidence we can provide:
- Audit log export showing delete request + replication events + expunge job runs.
- Signed manifest for snapshots excluded by hold.
- Drive link to the expunge runbook and post-run verification checklist.

Operational notes / constraints:
- If you have offsite immutable snapshots managed by a cloud provider that enforces a fixed retention window, we must respect that provider contract — we will surface exact retention dates for each snapshot as part of the evidence bundle.
- For regulatory notices, we recommend coordinating through a single POA (point of authority) in your org to avoid duplicate authorization delays.

Happy to walk through specifics on a quick call. If you want, we can run a short tabletop exercise with your compliance team to show the timeline and the evidence package.
